status: Read-only art and construction acceptance targets. Modeling remains paused. New equipment candidates have metadata screening; actual viewer review and source acquisition are separate gates.
primaryArtDirection: The existing individual Peris portrait is the target for face, clothing coverage, weapon, palette and pose. External references provide anatomy, surface quality and construction knowledge.

observations: Head is small relative to huge trapezius/shoulder and arm mass.
Brow, cheeks, nose, muzzle and teeth form a connected face; exposed muscle and hands are anatomical.
Iron rim, timber faces, leather wrapping, fur and skin are distinct physical surfaces, each with appropriate wear.
Rib/spine gaps remain open in profile; ribs connect into a coherent torso rather than hiding behind a pale human skin.
Shoulder/forearm plates have shell thickness, edging, straps and layer overlap; skeletal wrist/elbow remain legible.
Skull/horns share a connected anatomical base, with natural cavity depth and a genuine jaw profile.

acceptance: Side/front/rear views show pelvis on a padded seat, thighs actually straddling the mount, bent knees and feet supported at a plausible reachable position.
The saddle has a structural tree or pad, a continuous girth/harness, fastenings and clear attachment to the mount. A decorative ring or floating slab does not satisfy the seat.
Reins run from an actual bridle/bit to hands; straps avoid eyes, mouth and breathing space.
Inspect evaluated idle, walk and attack poses, including mixed rider/mount clips. Contact must remain coherent through motion rather than passing only bind-pose metadata.
Light scout, ordinary cavalry and heavy cavalry visibly differ in mount armor coverage, saddle load and rider kit while retaining the faction's portrait identity.
Distinct mammoth skull dome/shoulder hump, small ears, long trunk, curved tusks and shaggy belly/spine silhouette; anatomy reads from side as well as front.
Tusks emerge as a paired skull feature and have curved taper, not extra straight brown cones behind ivory replacements.
A howdah has visible load-bearing rails/deck/seat and a harness distributed over the actual back. The rider's feet sit on the deck and knees bend in a seated chair pose.
Orc and Pandaren platforms use their own approved iron/ochre versus jade/bronze/red construction; skeletal Undead retains actual bone negative space.
Wolf shows articulated long forelimbs/hocks, muzzle, shoulder blades and tail balance; boar has compact neck/shoulder mass, short legs, bristles, snout and anatomically rooted tusks.
Goat scout has true swept horns, beard, withers and cloven feet; stag has branched antlers and a graceful long-legged silhouette.
Saddle/rider pose changes with actual species and body width. Do not reuse one horse pelvis offset for every quadruped.
Match the primary portraits' scout mounts: Elf stag, Dwarf goat, Demon wolf. Record any mismatch with earlier roster text explicitly before construction.
Horse/mammoth skull, jaw, vertebrae, ribs, pelvis, scapula and limb ends have species-specific forms and real anatomical connections.
Bone thickness varies by structural purpose, with cavities and tendons/straps where needed. Uniform tubes and spherical gold joints fail the target.
Profile and rear leave rib/spine gaps visible; required saddle supports can bridge them but must not restore a smooth ivory living-animal torso.
At runtime inspection distance, the bones retain shape and texture. Hidden joints should use economical tessellation rather than raising formation cost without visible improvement.
Continuous undersuit/cuirass volume follows the actual race anatomy. Layered plates sit over it with intentional seams/overlaps; exposed skin appears only where the individual portrait exposes it.
Shoulder/neck/forearm/knee plates have deliberate shell thickness, edge bevels, straps and attachment. No floating collars, scattered plate patches, or chest holes caused by unrelated limb weights.
Armor is fitted against evaluated body surfaces and its animation articulation is reviewed visually. Rigid plate pieces follow the appropriate joint; cloth/hide uses smooth controlled deformation.

Iron, bronze, leather, wood, fur, jade and cloth have separate surface response and coherent scale. Wear follows exposed edges, friction, creases and impact locations rather than uniform procedural noise.
Open-faced portraits keep visible racial eyes, brow, muzzle, beard or ears. Historical source helmets and costumes cannot remain merely recolored beneath fantasy addons.
Closed boots/paw wraps/greaves cover or deliberately expose toes according to the portrait; no accidental retained Greek sandals.
The selected role weapon is recognizable from silhouette: a cutting axe blade, striking hammer face or long pike/glaive has a distinct geometry and length.
Visible blade bevel/edge thickness, socket/eye/fastening and grip wrapping support a real construction. A generic black box at the face is not a finished weapon.
Hands close around a reachable grip, with wrists and elbows supporting the weapon's mass. Guard/idle poses leave the approved face legible.
Match each individual portrait's ornament, scale, material and handedness before adding generic race motifs. Light roles cannot inherit the heavy elite weapon by default.
Bow has coherent limb curvature, a taut string, nocking point, hand grip and arrow flight path. Draw motion affects the actual limb/string rig while the grip remains at the hand socket.
Crossbow has a clear stock, transverse limbs, string, bolt rail, trigger and loading/foot support. It must not read as a thin hand-held bow.
A supporting hand holds the stock/fore-end and the firing hand reaches the grip/trigger; the projectile aligns with the rail and attack direction.
Dwarf/Gnome crossbow roles remove incompatible round shields and arrow quivers; carry bolt cases and loading tools matching the portrait.
Scout/light/heavy bow/crossbow variants differ in dimensions and construction, not just tint.

Gnome boar is constructed from segmented shells around an exposed chassis, with actual hinge/piston leg mechanisms, gears, rivets and cable/hose connections. Metallic paint on a live smooth boar fails.
Joint centers and piston endpoints form a plausible linkage and remain clear through animation; shell pieces provide clearance at knees, shoulders and neck.
Catapult/ram have actual beam joints, axles/wheels, lashing/iron straps, trigger/tension/windlass mechanisms and a clear projectile or striking path.
Gnome Gear Catapult's drive gears and brass axle/wheel assemblies are large enough to read at the game inspection scale; a tiny gear on a stock onager fails.
Living siege has a unique whole-body form and two-hand boulder support matched to the approved portrait; an anatomical human recolored grey does not make a stone/root giant.
The heavy beast has a barrel chest, low massive neck, broad muzzle, rooted horn and real weight-bearing legs/three-toed feet; it must read as its own species rather than a modified horse.
Demon plates/straps leave anatomical face folds, horn roots, ears, breathing space and leg clearance legible. Heavy saddle structure fits the real shoulder/back width.
Compare low-resolution gait and high-detail surface studies, then verify full rider/mount motion and portrait identity in actual game inspection.

reviewDeliverables: Actual reference viewer front, side, rear and three-quarter captures for selected primary studies; visible NoAI/provenance check recorded.
One portrait-matched finished unit hero candidate with neutral source closeups and actual Three.js unit inspection screenshots before propagating the approach.

Each role gets an individual art review against its own portrait and multiple views; file generation, clip counts and normalized weights are necessary technical checks but do not constitute artistic approval.
